correctness.rationale: Cloitre–Joshi Proposition 3.1 matches the exact greedy dyadic formula. On B=2^k, writing n=B+j, division yields h(1+j/B) plus exactly 1/[2(B+j)] for odd j on the first branch, and zero otherwise. The sublevel of h is the interval between inverse endpoints u(y) and v(y) on its range; its intersection with [1,θ] gives the stated additional mass and continuous CDF. The unnormalized numerator has mass θ. Each monotone branch contributes grid-count error at most one, and its inverse is 9-Lipschitz, so the strip of width 1/(2B) contains at most six grid points per branch. Thus each complete or truncated block contributes at most 14 count error. Complete block lengths total 2^K−4; the last block includes N and differs from the phase integral by one endpoint cell. Accounting for the initial three indices bounds the discrepancy by [14(K−1)+8]/N, certainly at most 30(K+1)/N. For j≤B/2, 4a(B+j)−3(B+j) is −j for even j and 2−j for odd j; for j>B/2 it is j−B. Only j=0 and 1 qualify in each block, plus n=1,2. The floor-log count is therefore exact, including cutoffs that are powers of two. The phase law has no atom at 3/4, so the left-hand CDF limit there supplies the lower bound without dropping the equality cases. Continuity in θ, compactness of [1,2], and integer cutoffs approaching each phase give all weak limits; for y=7/10 the first partial interval contributes zero on θ∈[1,5/4], so F_θ(y)=(5/12)/θ varies strictly there.
residual_risks: The finite threshold check is corroborative, not the proof. The upper constant is not optimized; sharpness is of order, not an exact leading Kolmogorov constant.

evidence: The dyadic formula directly singles out j=0 and j=1 as the endpoint exceptions and yields the limiting block profile h. Known mean subsequences match the mean of the phase pushforwards at θ=1 and 3/2.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The profile is available by rescaling, but the quantitative finding needs bounded block error simultaneously for every CDF threshold, accumulation across complete and truncated blocks, and endpoint control for a matching lower bound. It is not covered by the mean Riemann sums or by the exact arithmetic formula alone. If the words 'two limit points' in Theorem 7.1 are read as exhaustive for the mean, that reading is incompatible with its own dyadic formula: θ=11/10 gives (∫h+1/20+log(11/10)/4)/(11/10)≈0.71032, distinct from the two displayed values. The proof supplies the two subsequences, not their exhaustiveness.

originality.rationale: The arithmetic formula and pointwise oscillation are already known; the same paper also proves nonconvergence of the Cesàro mean and gives two explicit subsequential mean values, a stronger overlap than the frozen relationship section mentions. Neither those scalar means nor the inspected sequence entry and alternative Beatty solutions give the full weak-limit family or the uniform sharp-order phase-matched CDF estimate. The exact endpoint count is an elementary consequence of the existing formula and is credited principally as the mechanism forcing the new discrepancy lower bound, not as a new sequence formula.
residual_risks: The specific primary-literature query returned no additional relevant result; this is not negative proof of priority. Earlier equivalent distribution calculations outside the inspected sources are not ruled out. The frozen prior-work discussion should acknowledge the two previously computed Cesàro mean limits explicitly.

value.rationale: The result describes the fluctuation when pointwise and mean convergence fail: cutoff phase selects the whole probability law, and the exceptional ratios precisely force a logarithmic penalty missed by a single-block approximation.
